headline: Medium-risk pair: shared MCP/API surfaces and overlapping mutable workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of a critical default harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and REST/Python SDK, while OpenMetadata also exposes MCP, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. That creates a plausible shared-channel pathway where content from one can be ingested by the other, and the profiles do not show provenance isolation. The interaction is inferred from docs only, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MemMachine outputs are routed into OpenMetadata MCP tools or webhooks without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF OpenMetadata ingests MemMachine-generated text as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic tool execution on imported text.
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages.
Restrict MCP methods to read-only for the first test run.
Manually review any instruction-like content before forwarding.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts, preferences, and conversational context, and OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge. Both expose APIs and MCP surfaces, so a shared workspace or integration could move sensitive context between them. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, but the docs support a realistic leakage pathway, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF MemMachine context is exported into OpenMetadata catalogs, sensitive user facts may be retained there.
IF both agents are connected to the same workspace or webhook stream, data can flow beyond the original intended boundary.
mitigations: Limit shared fields to non-sensitive metadata.
Turn off verbose logging for cross-agent requests.
Review retention settings on both sides before connecting them.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction before export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can reach network egress and MCP, and OpenMetadata supports multiple instances plus APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. Even without explicit filesystem writes, both can mutate shared external resources through overlapping integration surfaces, so coordination conflicts are plausible. Because write-locking is not documented, uncertainty escalates from low to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same metadata or workflow endpoint, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF OpenMetadata instances are run concurrently against shared resources, MemMachine-triggered updates can race with catalog updates.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the writer for each resource.
Pause concurrent writes during initial integration testing.
Use idempotent update operations where available.
Check for existing locks or version fields before writing.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control at the shared resource layer.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can produce conversational context and long-term preferences, and OpenMetadata can consume and publish metadata, lineage, and governance information through APIs, events, and webhooks. If OpenMetadata treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors can propagate into catalog records or downstream automations. The pairwise handoff is inferred, not directly observed, so medium fits.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata uses MemMachine output without verification, incorrect facts can be propagated.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or events trigger actions from MemMachine-generated metadata, errors can cascade into downstream systems.
mitigations: Require human review for first-pass metadata imports.
Compare MemMachine output against source-of-truth records.
Disable auto-publish from MemMachine into OpenMetadata.
Log and diff every imported field before acceptance.
requires-engineering: add validation rules and confidence thresholds before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine is documented only as docs-only and touches long-term user facts and conversational context; OpenMetadata is verified and touches governance and lineage data. The profiles do not specify residency, certifications, or retention mismatches, so there is no concrete compliance breach shown. The risk is limited to a possible policy mismatch if the pair is configured to share regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from MemMachine into OpenMetadata without matching retention policy, a compliance gap exists.
IF either deployment has stricter residency or deletion requirements than the other, shared records may violate policy.
mitigations: Confirm both systems' retention settings.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared fields.
Document the data flow before enabling sync.
Review deletion/export procedures on both sides.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
